claim_matrix.boundary: Detection is limited to the exact immutable current-source projection.
Planning selects the repository-wide Source surface; upstream allowlists can still exclude selected paths from detector inspection.
Normalized content observations contain structural fields only.
PATH observations identify matching nonempty paths, not validated credential contents.
Identity uses validated non-secret structural evidence.
The frozen process contract bounds time and scanner output.
Timeout, cancellation, and output-limit outcomes cannot be represented as clean completed analysis.
Malformed, unsupported, or confidentiality-invalid scanner output fails without normalized findings.
Execution is bound to a verified immutable Source projection.
Two immediate runs had equal canonical structural sets for every frozen repository and the aggregate.
Canonical evidence excludes raw scanner streams, Secret, Match, and secret-derived public identity.
Frozen JSON evidence is deterministic, canonical, and content-addressed.
F3B covers seven representative detectors and F5 observed three rule IDs; neither establishes coverage of every inherited detector.
Upstream stopword, allowlist, and entropy behavior can suppress detector-shaped candidates.
The upstream directory source skips empty PKCS12 files.
Repository-wide selection does not imply inspection of bytes excluded by inherited Gitleaks path allowlists.
The 138 observations are sanitized structural detections without complete ground truth, credential validation, or exploitability review.
Evidence covers six frozen repositories and cannot represent all projects or repository shapes.
F3B metrics apply only to 48 frozen case/rule relations.
The integration supplies no network-dependent scanner configuration, but does not claim an operating-system network sandbox.
The frozen parser rejects unsupported Link or Fragment fields rather than silently accepting unmodeled output.
The frozen binding uses Gitleaks dir mode on the current snapshot only.
No credential is submitted to a provider.
Provider or API validation is outside Source v1.
A scanner observation is not exploitability evidence.
No control-flow or runtime credential reachability is evaluated.
Representative evidence and documented misses preclude an exhaustive claim.
F3B records three false negatives in its bounded corpus.
Bounded corpus metrics do not generalize to arbitrary repositories.
Acquisition is a separate controlled evidence phase, not scanner behavior.
This integration does not correlate Gitleaks findings with other tools.
Stable structural identity is not a cross-run lifecycle deduplication policy.
Two-run repeatability is not credential rotation tracking.
Only static current-snapshot source inspection is performed.

v0.4B.subject: execution lifecycle and bounded process semantics

final_limitation: This capability does not claim exhaustive secret detection, Git-history coverage, credential validity, exploitability, universal detector accuracy, or inspection of every selected byte. Upstream Gitleaks rules, allowlists, enumeration behavior, and supported output schema remain material limitations.

maturity_decision.future_benchmarked_requirement: A future BENCHMARKED state requires a broader frozen capability corpus covering a representative detector family set with explicit limitation-aware ground truth and repeatable scoring.
why_not_benchmarked: F3B measures seven representative detectors only.
F3B contains three documented false negatives.
F4 proves material upstream detector, enumeration, and path-allowlist limitations.
F5 has no complete frozen ground truth and therefore provides no accuracy score.
F5 observed only three rule IDs across the six frozen repositories.
Real-world repeatability proves structural determinism, not accuracy.

supported_claim: SecureScan Source v1 provides deterministic, current-snapshot secret detection through a pinned and verified Gitleaks 8.30.1 integration. Findings are parsed through a fail-closed confidentiality-preserving boundary and receive stable structural identities. Controlled benchmark, adversarial, acquisition, and real-world repeatability evidence are frozen and reproducible.
